newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks at four-month low despite bank flurry.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks at four-month low despite bank flurry.

text.p: Jordanian shares fell to a four-month low on Sunday despite a handful of bloc sales in banking shares which briefly lifted the market from the doldrums, brokers said.
The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index fell 0.35 percent to 150.93 points, its sixth fall in the last seven trading days.
"Local speculators are getting tired of the market," one broker said. "They've lost much of their capital and they've just got tired of it."
Early bloc trades in Jordan Islamic Bank and Jordan National Bank, which rose to 3.80 dinars and 1.90 dinars, helped lift the market initially.

The banks are two of the eight stocks on the exchange listed on International Finance Corporation's emerging market index and frequently attract institutional interest. Together they accounted for over three-quarters of Sunday's 787,000 dinar turnover ($1.1 million).
But both stocks slipped back in later trade. Jordan Islamic Bank closed down 0.03 dinars at 3.75 dinars and Jordan National Bank ended the day on 1.83 dinars, down 0.02.
"Most of the fundamentals are stable but people are very cautious now," said analyst Mohammad Abdallah of Pearl Investment.
Overall 24 shares fell while just eight rose. Another 11 were traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance fell 0.26 percent to 79.29 points, 4.92 percent down from the start of the year.
